justifications.c1: One independent per-incident figure (Global Foods £120k fine cut to £80k, search-confirmed) but it concerns chilled meat in a non-refrigerated truck, not a frozen-van fridge failure; load values (£5k, £25k) come from theft stories; no sourced spoilage write-off for a unit failure.
justifications.c2: Swiss cantonal campaign (search-confirmed): 17% of shipments ≥3 °C over limit, 35% in the 3.5–12 t class; Reg 37/2005 makes recording continuous per journey; but no UK per-van excursion or failure rate (recorded as not found).
justifications.c3: Paid incumbent workaround documented: EN 12830 printer recorders (Transcan, TouchPrint, eBay listing €379) and telematics add-ons at £18–30/vehicle/month (aggregators); driver labour on paper sheets not quantified.
justifications.c4: Primary statute Reg (EC) 37/2005 Art 2 requires recording instruments and ≥1-year dated record retention (search-confirmed on legislation.gov.uk) plus England/NI/Scotland regs; enforcement shown only for transport temperature control generally (Global Foods, Highland), none for the recording duty itself.
justifications.c5: Transport manager adverts (Fleet News UK; AU Coolways) tie the role to temperature compliance; budget ownership for the owner of a small independent distributor is not evidenced.
justifications.c6: Strong named channels already bundling monitoring for refrigerated vans: Marshall Fleet Solutions TempLog (trade press + Cold Chain Federation), CoolKit–ORBCOMM, Glacier loggers, GAH–Microlise; but these sell their own or partner products, so access for an entrant is unevidenced.
justifications.c7: Crowded category (Transcan, Carrier DataCOLD/ColdTrans, Thermo King, Microlise, ORBCOMM, Webfleet, RAM) and OEMs now pipe unit data to telematics; the small-fleet gap is asserted, with no complaints or pricing gap sourced.
justifications.c8: Teltonika EYE sensor with EN 12830 certificate at £37 and 12 V vehicle power evidenced, but the tracker/gateway is not priced and a new recorder needs EN 12830 conformity (calibration/traceability flag).
justifications.c9: Statutory ≥1-year record retention (Reg 37/2005) plus comparable subscriptions at £18–30/vehicle/month (≥£100/site/yr), though the price sources are aggregators rather than primary price lists.
justifications.c10: Regulator data (Swiss cantonal campaign), UK council enforcement news and STV news, but first-hand complaints are weak: a US forum header only and a paywalled AU tribunal title.

weakest: The market is crowded with EN 12830 recorders and fleet telematics, and refrigeration OEMs now feed unit temperature data straight into telematics, so the small-fleet gap is asserted rather than evidenced.
